In summary, our research is concerned with
the effect of diet and rumen inoculum preparation on rumen microbial dry weight and total bacterial and protozoal numbers.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chilling whole rumen contents and feeding a low energy diet (37% alfalfa and 63% concentrate) resulted in a rumen inoculum of the highest microbial activity for protein degradation.
chilling of whole rumen fluid enriched by particle-associated microorganisms is a superior inoculum preparation method for rumen fluid in vitro studies.
chilling of strained rumen contents prior inoculum preparation resulted in rumen microorganisms with the highest microbial numbers and protein degrading ability.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the microbial dry weight, bacterial counts, protozoal counts and fractional degradation rates were higher in rumen contents from ruminants fed diets high in protein and/or energy.
rumen microbial numbers are affected by both diet and inoculum preparation.
rumen inoculum prepared by chilling strained rumen fluid prior to addition of particle-associated microorganisms is the most suitable for use in in vitro incubations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
rumen inoculum preparation and diet affect the numbers and activities of microbes in the rumen.
microbial dry weight and total bacterial counts were not good indicators of rumen microbial protein degradation activity.
rumen inoculum preparation can affect rumen microbial numbers.
